claude.sample_unit: TCM practitioners (plus 160 exam questions, 30 cases, 5 clinical cases for human-AI comparison)

links.outcome: Decision quality and time for physicians with vs without LLM assistance
links.effect: Human-AI collaboration scored 33.62 vs physician-only 28.97 (P<.001), 66.1% time reduction (162.6 s vs 479.2 s); AI-only 33.80, not different from collaboration (P=.79).
links.quote: Pairwise comparisons revealed that human-AI collaboration significantly outperformed physician-only decision-making (paired t 49 =6.603, Cohen d =0.943; P< .001), representing a 116.1% quality improvement.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI in workflow versus standalone AI and physician alone
links.effect: Collaboration 33.62 (SD 2.50) vs physician-only 28.97 (SD 4.94) vs AI-only 33.80 (SD 1.12); no significant difference between AI-only and collaboration (P=.79).
links.quote: No significant difference was observed between AI-only and human-AI collaboration groups ( t 49 =−0.271, Cohen d =−0.074; P= .79), while AI-only significantly outperformed physician-only approaches ( t 49 =−5.358, Cohen d =−1.015; P< .001).

links.outcome: Comparison of five LLMs against each other on TCM knowledge and case analysis for model selection
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 had 96.7% knowledge accuracy vs 50.6-66.3% for others, and 17.31/20 case score vs 10.02-16.16; chosen as optimal model (P<.001).
links.quote: Based on superior performance across both evaluation domains and a significant advantage of 15.89 points over the second-ranked model, DeepSeek-R1 was selected as the optimal model for phase 4 clinical application and human-AI collaboration assessment.

links.outcome: Output reproducibility across repeated runs and model consistency
links.effect: Triple repetition; Fleiss kappa 0.969 DeepSeek-R1, 0.953 Gemini, 0.764 Claude, 0.803 GPT-4.5, 0.614 Grok3; case-score SDs across attempts 0.55-2.04.
links.quote: Internal consistency analysis using Fleiss κ demonstrated excellent reliability for DeepSeek-R1 (κ=0.969) and Gemini 2.0 (κ=0.953), with moderate to good reliability for other models—Claude 3.7 (κ=0.764), GPT-4.5 (κ=0.803), and Grok3 (κ=0.614).

links.outcome: Physician adoption, modification, and rejection of AI-generated plans after review
links.effect: Of 400 decisions, 74.25% adopted, 24% modified, 1.75% rejected; medication recommendations had 32% adoption and 62% modification.
links.quote: Collaboration pattern analysis across 400 total decisions revealed high acceptance rates—74.25% (297/400) adoption, 24% (96/400) modification, and 1.75% (7/400) rejection.

links.outcome: LLM TCM clinical knowledge accuracy, error patterns including formula misuse
links.effect: Non-DeepSeek models had error rates 33.8%-49.4%; formula misuse was the most common error; accuracy on advanced questions fell (Claude 85.6% to 37.5%).
links.quote: Error pattern analysis indicated that “formula misuse” was the most common error type across all models, followed by “theory knowledge deficits” and “syndrome differentiation inaccuracy.”

links.outcome: Exam-based LLM performance versus real-world clinical competence
links.effect: Authors state exam-case results may not translate to real clinical settings, which involve incomplete information and diagnostic uncertainty.
links.quote: These factors suggest that the observed performance levels may not directly translate to real-world clinical settings, although this represents an essential first step before clinical validation studies.

unlisted_practices: Weighted composite scoring with sensitivity analysis of weighting schemes for model selection
System Usability Scale assessment of clinician acceptance of LLM decision support

links.outcome: clinician performance with AI
links.quote: Human-AI collaboration achieved significant improvements compared with physician-only decision-making, with 16.1% quality enhancement (33.62 vs 28.97; P<.001) and 66.1% time reduction (162.6 s vs 479.2 s; P<.001).

links.outcome: candidate model comparison
links.effect: Comprehensive scores: DeepSeek-R1 90.61, Gemini 74.72, Claude 70.23, Grok3 57.44, GPT-4.5 51.06.
links.quote: DeepSeek-R1 achieved the highest comprehensive score of 90.61 points, followed by Gemini 2.0 (74.72 points), Claude 3.7 (70.23 points), Grok3 (57.44 points), and GPT-4.5 (51.06 points).

links.outcome: repeated-run output stability
links.effect: Stability varied: SD 0.55 Gemini, 0.69 DeepSeek, 1.13 Claude, 1.99 GPT-4.5, 2.04 Grok3.
links.quote: Model output stability analysis across multiple attempts revealed varying degrees of consistency, with Gemini 2.0 demonstrating the highest stability (mean 16.16, SD 0.55), followed by DeepSeek-R1 (mean 17.31, SD 0.69), Claude 3.7 (mean 14.57, SD 1.13), GPT-4.5 (mean 10.02, SD 1.99), and Grok3 (mean 12.40, SD 2.04).

links.outcome: expert-rating reliability
links.effect: Total scores ICC=0.987 (95% CI 0.980‐0.990); Western diagnosis and safety ICC=1.000.
links.quote: ICC revealed perfect agreement for Western diagnosis (ICC=1.000) and safety considerations (ICC=1.000), with near-perfect agreement for precautions (ICC=0.997, 95% CI 1.000‐1.000) and total scores (ICC=0.987, 95% CI 0.980‐0.990).

links.outcome: clinician usability
links.effect: System Usability Scale mean 76.8 (SD 5.9), range 65.0‐87.5.
links.quote: System Usability Scale evaluation yielded positive results with a mean score of 76.8 (SD 5.9, range 65.0‐87.5).

links.outcome: clinician review changes
links.effect: Across 400 decisions: 74.25% adopted, 24% modified, 1.75% rejected.
links.quote: Collaboration pattern analysis across 400 total decisions revealed high acceptance rates—74.25% (297/400) adoption, 24% (96/400) modification, and 1.75% (7/400) rejection.

links.outcome: TCM answer errors
links.effect: DeepSeek-R1 total error rate 3.3%; other models ranged 33.8%-49.4%.
links.quote: DeepSeek-R1 maintained the lowest error rates across all error categories (total error rate=3.3%), while other models had error rates ranging from 33.8% (Claude 3.7) to 49.4% (Grok3).

links.outcome: clinical decision-making quality score
links.effect: no significant difference between AI-only and human-AI collaboration (33.80 vs 33.62; t49=-0.271, P=.79)
links.quote: No significant difference was observed between AI-only and human-AI collaboration groups ( t 49 =−0.271, Cohen d =−0.074; P= .79), while AI-only significantly outperformed physician-only approaches ( t 49 =−5.358, Cohen d =−1.015; P< .001).
